analyst_view.overall: Juventus are 5th with 10 points and unbeaten in Europe, and a win would put them close to a top-eight place; Omonia (18th, 6 points) are in the play-off places but lost their last European game 3-1 at NEC. Luciano Spalletti goes to Como on Sunday and Tuttosport says he may change up to eight players from the Venezia win: Conceicao (over his shoulder problem), Sarr, Boga, McKennie, Gatti and Cambiaso are tipped to start, with Kolo Muani or Woltemade up front. Yildiz, Locatelli, Thuram, Grabara and Adzic are out, Zhegrova is unavailable and Sports Mole now expects Alajbegovic to miss out with a thigh problem; the numbers only take something off for Locatelli. Omonia under Henning Berg are without Carel Eiting, have Loic Nego back and Lois Diony has scored in three straight games. English referee Samuel Barrott (about 4.0 cards a game) is already counted. An evening check found no confirmed lineup yet and nothing that changes the morning's rotation news, so the view stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (Juventus 2.0) and take only a little off for Locatelli. They do not see Yildiz's absence or a side with up to eight changes before Como, and Alajbegovic now looks likely to miss out too, so I go lower, to about 2.7; Diony's form for Omonia keeps the cut small.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, mostly Juventus (8.1), already up for their 44 corners in the last six games. Omonia will defend deep, which the split already shows, but a reshuffled Juventus without Yildiz should pin them back a little less, so I shade it to about 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already trimmed because Juventus have drawn few bookings lately (5 in six) and Omonia have been calm, with referee Samuel Barrott close to average (4.0 a game). A one-sided game with Omonia defending tends to stay quiet and rotation does not change that, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.7 shots, with Omonia's recent shooting already adding about 15% to their side. A Juventus side with many changes and no Yildiz should create a bit less than the usual first team, so I go to about 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, 7.6 of them for Juventus. With Yildiz out and the attack rebuilt around Conceicao, Boga, McKennie and Kolo Muani or Woltemade, Juventus's finishing should be a little less sharp, so I go to about 9.7.
